Only differences from the reader's quote are whitespace: the slide title has a double space before the dash and the low-level alternants '[kóí bà]/' and '[kòì↓bà]' sit on two l…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Porome is described as a tone language with five lexical word-tone melodies (high-level, low-level, rising, falling, peaking) distinguishing minimal pairs such as kóí 'cloth' vs kòì 'selfish' and mèrí 'road' vs mérì 'pandanus'; the source says nothing about stress or accent placement. Velasquez 2022 independently marks Kibiri lexemes with word melodies (HL, LH, HH, H, L) and is likewise silent on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; tone realisation is shown to vary with following context (e.g. low-level /kòì/ realised [kóí bà] or [kòì↓bà] before the copula bá, with downstep).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone melodies illustrated on citation forms and in a two-word frame ('It is a..' / 'It is not a..'); the frames show phrase-level tonal interaction (downstep, level adjustments), which Petterson does not analyse. Slides from a conference talk, not a peer-reviewed phonology; Velasquez's in-progress Sorbonne Nouvelle grammar of Kibiri-Porome is expected to supersede it.
new_statements.identity_note: Petterson 2019 describes the Porome dialect (Ero village; Glottolog dialect poro1255 under kibi1239), whose speakers Petterson worked with for SIL; Velasquez 2022 describes Kibiri proper (Kikori, Babeio, Veiru, Doibo; Glottolog dialect aird1238 'Aird Hills'). Franklin 1975 treats Porome and Kibiri as two closely related dialects of one language; Velasquez notes structural distinctions between them are not yet well defined. Both sources agree on lexical word tone; neither says anything about stress.

sources.locator: slide 6 'Tones - 5 word tone patterns' (PDF page 7); cf. slide 5 'Sounds - 5 vowels + 9 consonants' (PDF page 6)
sources.note: Slide 5 (PDF p. 6) gives 5 vowels + 9 consonants; slide 6 (PDF p. 7) 'Tones - 5 word tone patterns' lists High-level /kóí/ 'cloth', Low-level /kòì/ 'selfish', Rising /mèrí/ 'road', Falling /mérì/ 'pandanus', Peaking /pàkúmì/ 'feather' and says 'All other neighbouring languages also tonal (except Baimuru)'. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 30 slides; no statement on stress placement.

Phonology section (consonants, 5 vowels, 5 tones) is copied entirely from Petterson 2019 slides 5-6; no stress statement. Used only to confirm the source trail (Petterson 2010 picture dictionary; Petterson 2019).

sources.citation: Velasquez, Moisés. 2022. Preserving the unheard, promoting the unspoken: The challenges of documenting, preserving and promoting Kibiri, a critically endangered isolate. Handout, 54th LSPNG Conference, UPNG, Port Moresby, 21-22 Sept 2022, 9 pp. (Glottolog ref 668630, listed by Glottolog as a minimal description; also HAL hal-03913233).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 2 'Phonology' heading followed by a lexeme list with word-tone melodies (e.g. /dɔ HL/ '2SG', /mu(:)ɾi LH/ 'knee', /mɛɾi HL/ 'path', /ki:mi HH/ 'head', /kumi HH/ 'dog', /vɛi L/ 'bone', /pɔu H/ 'to come'); the consonant/vowel charts are images with no text layer. Nothing on stress or accent; the rest of the handout is on verbal number and construct forms.
